sla_negotiation_summary: Requested uptime: Saltmarsh legal prefers 99.99% monthly uptime; engineering says 99.95% is typical for dedicated pools
Credit schedule asked by Saltmarsh: tiered credits with faster escalations (10% for <99.95, 25% for <99.9, 50% for <99.8) — Redwood proposed: 10% for <99.95, 30% for <99.9, 100% for <99.0
Maintenance windows: Saltmarsh requests pre-approved quarterly maintenance with max 2 hours per window, preferred local time: 02:00-04:00 ET
Support SLAs requested: P1 response 15 min, on-call pager; P2 response 2 hours; P3 24 hours. Redwood proposed P1 30 min during business hours + on-call for P1 outside hours
RTO/RPO expectations: Saltmarsh wants documented rollback and fallback policies to avoid model degradation during maintenance
Data residency: Saltmarsh requires US-EAST residency and guaranteed no cross-region failover without notice
technical_requirements: Reserved capacity plan: initial 8x A100-80GB equiv reserved (target steady throughput: 150 QPS chat, 25k tokens/sec batch embeddings)
Burst policy: capability to burst +50% for 30m windows twice per day — need pricing clarity
Latency SLOs: p95 token latency target <= 250ms for chat with 2k token context; p99 target <= 600ms
Throughput guarantees: sustained 150 QPS with 95% success rate during business hours; plan for autoscale handoff and warm KV cache
Model versions: pin to curated open LLM v2.1; automatic fallback to quantized variant acceptable for capacity constraints
poc_plan: 30-day reserved pool (8 GPUs) - validate throughput and p95 latency against production trace
Week 1: baseline profiling and kernel selection; Week 2: latency stress tests (peak QPS); Week 3: reliability injection (node reboots, maintenance sim); Week 4: cost/runbook review and final report
Success criteria: p95 <=250ms at 150 QPS, sustained throughput >= promised tokens/sec, no data residency violations
Deliverables: performance report, cost forecast, recommended reserved sizing and fallback policy
